scenes.text: They look. They leave. Leo wonders why. Meet Leo, a furniture shop owner. Every day, people browse and walk away. He has clues: what they looked at, almost bought, and paid for. But those clues sit in different places. His next offer is still a guess. Who should he reach, and with what?

scenes.text: It starts by connecting the clues. Our ontology connects shoppers, products, contacts and payments, so each prediction uses the right examples. Recommendations stay separate from inquiries. One rule: past signals become inputs; later outcomes become labels. The model can't peek into the future.

scenes.text: With that map, the agent studies demand and stock, selects twenty eight days of history, and asks local tools to train two models. Every choice is saved in a checkpoint.
